EyHVzGS3zhJ2495jsZiKXg.zh: 沙烏地阿拉伯今年截至4月累計報告2例病例,其中1例死亡,病患皆為成年男性,感染來源仍不明,該國去(2025)年累計報告17 例。全球自2012年4月迄今累計報告2,649例確定病例及960例死亡病例。歐洲CDC評估歐盟/歐洲經濟區傳播風險為低。
EyHVzGS3zhJ2495jsZiKXg.en: Saudi Arabia reported two cases cumulatively as of April this year, one of which was fatal. All patients were adult men, and the source of infection remains unknown. The country reported 17 cases in total last year (2025). Globally, since April 2012, 2,649 confirmed cases and 960 deaths have been reported cumulatively. ECDC assesses the risk of transmission in the EU/EEA as low.

YtJ4XzfPsm1w52s1IYEDYA.zh: 全球今(2025)年截自12/21累計報告19例確定病例,其中4例死亡,病患主要分布於沙烏地阿拉伯(17例),另法國通報2例旅遊相關境外移入病例;沙國於6/4-12/21報告7例確定病例,其中2例死亡,分布於中部利雅德省(3例)、西南部奈季蘭省(2例)及西部塔伊夫市(2例)等地,病患間無流行病學關聯;法國於12月報告2例確定病例,皆有阿拉伯半島旅遊史,已完成接觸者追蹤,無次級感染情形。WHO表示病毒仍持續在單峰駱駝中循環,致偶發動物傳人事件,目前尚無疫苗或特效治療藥物,以支持性照護為主,另醫療照護環境是人傳人感染的主要風險場域,建議各國加強急性呼吸道感染監測、落實感染管制措施,並提醒高風險族群避免接觸駱駝及其產品,評估全球及區域風險維持為中。
YtJ4XzfPsm1w52s1IYEDYA.en: Globally in 2025, as of 21 December, 19 confirmed cases had been reported cumulatively, including 4 deaths. Most were in Saudi Arabia (17 cases), and France reported 2 travel-related imported cases. Saudi Arabia reported 7 confirmed cases between 4 June and 21 December, including 2 deaths, distributed across Riyadh province in central Saudi Arabia (3 cases), Najran province in the southwest (2) and the city of Taif in the west (2), with no epidemiological link between patients. France reported 2 confirmed cases in December, both with travel history to the Arabian Peninsula; contact tracing has been completed and no secondary infection was found. WHO said the virus continues to circulate in dromedary camels, causing occasional animal-to-human transmission. There is currently no vaccine or specific treatment, and care is mainly supportive. Healthcare settings are the main risk setting for human-to-human transmission. WHO recommends that countries strengthen surveillance of acute respiratory infections, implement infection prevention and control measures, and remind high-risk groups to avoid contact with camels and their products. WHO assesses the global and regional risk as moderate.

pmPhKmmuKk6Vq-hrz062kQ.zh: 法國新增2例境外移入病例,病患曾同行至阿拉伯半島旅行,於出現疑症狀後確診,目前住院治療中,病況皆穩定,當局表示已啟動防治措施,旅行團成員健康監測中,目前尚未發現次級感染病例;該國迄今僅2013年通報2例境外移入病例,另全球迄今累計逾2千例,其中,沙烏地阿拉伯占84%病例,該病毒主要動物宿主為單峰駱駝,病例多與接觸駱駝有關,另曾出現醫護人員於接觸病人後感染之案例。
pmPhKmmuKk6Vq-hrz062kQ.en: France reported 2 new imported cases. The patients had travelled together to the Arabian Peninsula; they were diagnosed after developing suspicious symptoms and are now hospitalised in stable condition. Authorities have activated prevention and control measures, and members of the tour group are under health monitoring. No secondary cases have been found so far. France had previously reported only 2 imported cases, in 2013. Globally, more than 2,000 cases have been reported cumulatively, of which Saudi Arabia accounts for 84%. The main animal host is the dromedary camel, and cases are mostly associated with contact with camels. There have also been cases in which healthcare workers were infected after contact with patients.

Lf9xx7OEN6K_drXbKQ6t8Q.zh: 沙烏地阿拉伯於3/13報告11例,病患皆於今年1-3月中旬曾前往沙國朝覲,診斷時間介於1/7-3/2間,均未接種疫苗,病患於該國接受治療後,已康復出院,經檢驗為腦膜炎雙球菌W135血清型;另有6例零星個案返國就醫,其中2例檢出W135血清型。WHO表示朝覲等大型宗教活動人數眾多,且長時間近距離接觸,大幅提高腦膜炎雙球菌等呼吸道疾病傳播風險。當局評估今年截至3月上旬,僅54%朝覲者接種疫苗,因各國旅客前往沙國進行宗教活動,國際傳播風險上升。鑑於近期與朝覲相關病例增加,WHO呼籲預計參加活動者,應於出發至少10日前接種疫苗,以降低感染及傳播風險。
Lf9xx7OEN6K_drXbKQ6t8Q.en: Saudi Arabia reported 11 cases on 13 March. All patients had visited Saudi Arabia for the Hajj pilgrimage between January and mid-March this year, with diagnosis dates between 7 January and 2 March. None had been vaccinated. After treatment in Saudi Arabia, the patients recovered and were discharged; testing identified Neisseria meningitidis serotype W135. Another 6 sporadic cases returned home for medical care, 2 of which were confirmed as serotype W135. WHO said that large religious gatherings such as the Hajj, with large numbers of people and prolonged close contact, greatly increase the risk of transmission of respiratory diseases such as meningococcal meningitis. Authorities assessed that as of early March this year, only 54% of pilgrims had been vaccinated; as travellers from various countries go to Saudi Arabia for religious activities, the international transmission risk has increased. Given the recent rise in Hajj-related cases, WHO calls on those planning to attend to get vaccinated at least 10 days before departure to reduce the risk of infection and transmission.
